suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-9 adds this relationship only as a bounded clinical proposition. Chronic pancreatitis is associated with a substantially increased subsequent risk of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, with risk increasing with disease duration. Primary phenotype must be chronic pancreatitis, not an isolated acute-pancreatitis episode. Require separately established pancreatic cancer and chronology compatible with cancer developing after chronic pancreatitis. Do not infer cancer from pancreatitis alone. Preserve hereditary syndromes, smoking, age, diabetes, obesity, alcohol exposure, other pancreatic-cancer risk factors, and the possibility that occult pancreatic cancer initially presented as pancreatitis. The cited literature supports only this constrained relationship and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
